title: Apply a change set to the relay role matrix in one atomic write
lead: *Proposed.* `slicer relay-roles apply` reads a JSON change set (a list of the existing edit verbs as objects), checks every step against a copy of the matrix, and either refuses the whole set or saves it once, under one project lock. `relay-roles show --json` gains a `revision` that a change set can name as `expect`, so a tool never applies a change on top of a matrix it did not read. `--dry-run` prints the result and writes nothing.
findings_note: ork owner request 2026-11-02: unify settings across ork, slicer and adj; a tool sets up the matrix per project through slicer's own commands
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the whole-matrix replace form (the next item, `relay-roles-replace`, which builds on this one), new matrix roles for the UI pass or spec check, a user-level (global) default matrix, any change to `recommend`, to the schema of `relay-roles.json` (stays 3) or to the merge driver, and any ork code.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
ork (a sibling tool that runs slice relays) wants the owner to set up each project's role matrix from ork's UI, CLI or an AI workflow, while slicer stays the only writer of `.slicer/relay-roles.json` (`AGENTS.md`: "Change `.slicer/relay-roles.json` only through `slicer relay-roles`"). Today a tool can do that only one verb per process: `add`, `set`, `remove`, `move`, `rule-add`, `rule-edit` and `rule-remove` each take the lock, save and record history on their own (`src/slicer/ops.py:3362-3506`). That has three costs for a tool:

- No atomic change. Adding a row and moving it into place is two writes; if the second is refused, the matrix is left half changed. The owner's 2026-11-02 Grok rows (r21-r24, `relay-roles add` four times) are the shape of change a tool needs to make in one step.
- No validated preview. A tool can show the argv it will run, but not slicer's verdict on it, until it runs it.
- No lost-update guard. `show --json` returns `{relay_roles, rows, rules}` (`src/slicer/cli.py:636-645`) with no revision, so a tool cannot tell that the matrix changed between its read and its write (an owner edit in another terminal, a merge).

The pieces exist: every verb validates before it saves (`_check_role`, `_parse_scores`, `_parse_yes_no_any`, `_reject_bad_role_text`, `_rule_text` in `ops.py`), `RoleMatrix` is a dataclass with `to_dict` (`src/slicer/roles.py:229-285`), and `snapshot.revision` already hashes a JSON value to 12 hex digits (`src/slicer/snapshot.py:14-15`). "Import and migration stay all-or-nothing" is an invariant in `AGENTS.md`; this applies the same rule to the matrix.

Interface (*proposed*; an implementer records the details PROJECT.md leaves open with `slicer catalog add --kind decision`):

- `slicer relay-roles show --json` adds `revision` (12 hex digits, `snapshot.revision(matrix.to_dict())`, so it covers rows, rules, order and both counters) after `rules`. Additive; `--lean` keeps it.
- `slicer relay-roles apply (--file PATH | --stdin) [--dry-run] [--json] [--lean] [--render] [--strict]`. Input is one JSON object: `{"expect": "REVISION"?, "ops": [OP, ...]}`. `ops` is non-empty. Each OP is one object with an `op` key:
  - `{"op": "add", "role": R, "ref": "NAME"?, FIELDS}`
  - `{"op": "set", "id": ID, FIELDS}` (only the fields given; `""` clears a text field, `[]` or `"any"` clears a condition, as the flags do)
  - `{"op": "remove", "id": ID}`
  - `{"op": "move", "id": ID, "before": ID}` or `{"op": "move", "id": ID, "last": true}`
  - `{"op": "rule-add", "text": T, "ref": "NAME"?}`, `{"op": "rule-edit", "id": ID, "text": T}`, `{"op": "rule-remove", "id": ID}`
  - FIELDS are the `add`/`set` flag names with `_` for `-`: `size`, `effort`, `importance`, `urgency` (lists), `well_specified`, `split`, `sliver` (`yes`, `no` or `any`), `agent`, `vendor`, `model`, `reasoning`, `note` (strings). Unknown keys are refused.
  - An `id` or `before` of `@NAME` names the row or rule an earlier `add` or `rule-add` in the same set gave `"ref": "NAME"`, so "add a row and move it before r9" is one set.
- Steps apply in order to an in-memory copy. Every step is checked; all problems are collected (as `import` does) and the whole set is refused with nothing written, each problem naming its step (`ops[3]: no such relay role row: r99`). With `expect` given and not equal to the current revision, the set is refused with a new code `stale_revision` (exit 2) before any step runs.
- A step that changes nothing (a `set` to the current value, a `move` to the current place) is `changed: false`, as `set` and `move` are today. A set whose steps all change nothing writes nothing and exits 0, so applying the same set twice is safe.
- On success: one `save_roles`, one history entry per changed step through `_record_role` (the same `action`, `item` and notes the single verbs write), then `--render` as other writes do.
- `--json` result: `{"dry_run": bool, "changed": bool, "revision_before": R, "revision": R2, "steps": [{"op", "id", "changed"}], "rows": [...], "rules": [...]}` where `id` is the real id (the one allocated for an `add`), and `rows`/`rules` are the matrix after the set, as `show --json` prints them. `--dry-run` returns the same with `dry_run: true`, takes no lock, writes nothing and records nothing. `--lean` keeps `steps`, `rows` and `rules` even when empty.
- Error codes: existing `unknown_role_row`, `unknown_role_rule`, `bad_role_field`, `usage` for a malformed set (not JSON, no `ops`, unknown `op` or key, both or neither of `before` and `last`, a `@NAME` with no earlier `ref`, a duplicate `ref`), and the new `stale_revision`.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/roles.py` (a `revision(matrix)` helper beside `RoleMatrix`, or reuse `snapshot.revision`; the change-set parser and its dataclasses if they are pure, no I/O).
- `src/slicer/ops.py` (a `roles_apply(state, change_set, *, dry_run)` beside `role_add` at `:3362`; it reuses the per-verb checks on a copy of `state.roles` and saves once; split the existing verbs' bodies into check-and-apply helpers so the single verbs and `apply` share one code path).
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`cmd_relay_roles_show` at `:636-645` adds `revision`; a new `cmd_relay_roles_apply`; `radd("apply", ..., mutate=True)` beside `:4729-4785`, with `--file`, `--stdin` and `--dry-run`; a dry run must not take the project lock, see how `import --dry-run` does it at `:1422-1456`).
- `tests/test_relay_roles.py` (new cases on `RelayRolesCase`, which has `with_matrix`, `ok`, `refuse`, `matrix`, `snapshot` and `history` at `:26-66`).
- `docs/commands.md` (the `relay-roles show` row at `:66` and the Relay roles section at `:751`: the new command).
- `docs/agents.md` (the `relay-roles show` JSON row at `:576`, the edit verbs at `:579`, and the error-code table near `:825-840`: `stale_revision`).
- `CHANGELOG.md` (an entry under the unreleased heading).
- This project's matrix is not changed by this slice.

Overlap: s311 (Split `cli.py` and `ops.py`, L, open) moves the same files; land one before the other.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `tests/test_relay_roles.py`, named in the house style:

- `test_RelayRolesShow_Json_HasARevisionThatChangesWithEveryWrite`: `show --json` has a 12-hex `revision`; after `set r1 --model x` it differs; after `set r1 --model x` again (no change) it is the same. Fails first: no key.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_AddThenMoveByRef_OneSaveOneHistoryEntryPerStep`: `{"ops": [{"op":"add","role":"reviewer","agent":"Grok","vendor":"xAI","model":"latest","ref":"g"}, {"op":"move","id":"@g","before":"r1"}]}` gives the new row first, `steps[0].id` is the allocated id, the file was written once (patch `State.save_roles` to count), and history has an `add` and a `move` entry. Fails first: no `apply` command (exit 2 `usage`).
- `test_RelayRolesApply_OneBadStep_RefusesTheWholeSetAndWritesNothing`: a valid `set` followed by `{"op":"remove","id":"r99"}` exits 2 with `unknown_role_row`, the message names `ops[1]`, and `snapshot()` is byte-identical before and after.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_CollectsEveryProblem`: two bad steps report both, in step order.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_StaleExpect_IsRefusedBeforeAnyStep`: `expect` from an earlier `show`, then a `set` by another command, then `apply` exits 2 with `stale_revision` and writes nothing; the matching revision applies.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_DryRun_ReturnsTheResultAndWritesNothing`: `--dry-run --json` returns `dry_run: true`, the would-be `rows` and `revision`, no history entry, no lock file contention (run it while another test holds the project lock and see it succeed), and a byte-identical `snapshot()`.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_SameSetTwice_SecondIsNoChange`: a set of `set` steps applied twice: the second returns `changed: false`, every step `changed: false`, and writes nothing.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_SameValidationAsTheSingleVerbs`: a bad role, an effort of 4, a `well_specified` of `maybe`, a blank rule text, a newline in a note: each is refused with the same code the matching single verb gives.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_MalformedSet_IsUsage`: not JSON, no `ops`, empty `ops`, unknown `op`, unknown key, `move` with both or neither of `before` and `last`, an unknown or duplicate `ref`, both `--file` and `--stdin`.
- `test_RelayRolesApply_Render_LikeOtherWrites`: `--render` rewrites `RELAY-ROLES.md` once; `--strict` refuses when the render fails, as for `add`.
- `test_RelayRolesSingleVerbs_Unchanged`: the existing verb tests keep passing (no edit to them).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Begin in a new worktree `/Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/slicer/.worktrees/<id>` on a new feature branch from main, before claiming. Keep the working directory at `/Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/slicer`; use `git -C` and `PYTHONPATH=.worktrees/<id>/src python3 -m slicer --root .worktrees/<id>`.
2. Write the failing tests and see each fail for the reason given.
3. Refactor each matrix verb in `ops.py` into a check step and an apply step on a `RoleMatrix` value, with no I/O, and keep the public `role_add` and friends as thin wrappers that load, apply, save and record. No behavior change for the single verbs.
4. Add `roles_apply`: copy the matrix (`RoleMatrix.from_dict(m.to_dict())`), check `expect`, run each step's check and apply on the copy, resolve `@NAME` refs to the ids allocated on the copy, collect problems, and refuse with all of them, or save once and record history per changed step. A dry run stops before the save and takes no lock.
5. `show --json` adds `revision`. `apply` prints the result shape above; the text form lists one line per step (`added r25`, `moved r25`, `r5 unchanged`) and the new revision.
6. Docs and the error-code table; mark the command *proposed* in the CHANGELOG entry.
7. Do not change the file schema, the merge driver, `recommend`, the TUI, or this project's matrix.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` with the worktree's ignored TMPDIR (over 180 s; run it in the background).
- `slicer check` and `git diff --check` in the worktree.
- In a scratch project under `.venv/test-tmp` (`slicer init --relay-roles`): `relay-roles show --json` shows `revision`; `relay-roles apply --stdin --dry-run --json` with the add-then-move set prints the would-be matrix and leaves `git status` clean; the same without `--dry-run` writes once.
- Hand off with `handoff --render --check`; commit on the worktree branch only; merging waits for the owner.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice's feature branch: "relay-roles apply: atomic change sets with a revision guard". Merging, pushing and publishing wait for the owner.
